conclusion: A valid 50-row consecutive-Z raster preserves maximum-recovery contour data, inferred gaps and uncertainty. Some localized CT correspondence survives small-lag diagnostics, but substantial path-length/order instability and irregular misregistration prevent broad fine-scale coherence. This is neither a PASS nor evidence that every neighboring row is unrelated.
visual_observations: The authoritative raw and globally contrasted overviews show short patches of approximately vertical or diagonal intensity agreement, but predominantly interrupted, row-specific texture rather than long persistent fine structures. Right-tail coverage changes abruptly between rows. The zero-shift local map alternates positive and negative regions. Local best-lag plots show stronger selected correspondence, including shared broad valleys/peaks in the disclosed examples, but the lag map is irregular and matched-control exceedances are sparse. No stable global shear is apparent. Missing CT remains visibly masked; neither bridge filling nor a registered raster was created.
limitations: The fixed coarse ridge graph can fuse or switch apparent layers; high observed-ridge utilization is not certification of physical sheet identity. Forty-five rows are topology-clean; five retain one residual defect and are flagged rather than repaired post hoc. Independent seed positions, branch choices, different path orders, and inferred distances can all disturb s correspondence. Diagnostics cannot uniquely attribute every discontinuity to one cause. Strong windows were selected after evaluation and are not typical performance. The learned/3-D alternatives and text readability were not tested.
next_proposed: A separately authorized bounded investigation of per-slice seed/order and topology robustness would be more informative than immediately extending the unchanged method to a larger Z span. No such follow-up was performed.
